blocks.content: Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and subsequent cementation of material at the Earth's surface and within bodies of water.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Formed by the accumulation, compaction, and cementation of mineral and organic particles over geological time.
Characterized by distinct bedding planes or strata, making them stratified rocks.
Only rock type that contains fossils, offering vital clues about earth's prehistoric climate and evolution.
Categorized into mechanically formed (clastic), organically formed, and chemically formed rocks.

rows: Compaction and cementation of weathered pre-existing rock fragments
Accumulation and compaction of plant and animal organic debris
Precipitation of dissolved minerals from water bodies through evaporation

items: Fossils are found exclusively in sedimentary rocks; igneous and metamorphic processes destroy organic remains.
Shale is the most abundant sedimentary rock, accounting for over 50% of all sedimentary rocks on Earth's crust.
Limestone can form either organically through skeletal remains or chemically through calcite precipitation.
